response.response:
{
  "research_question": "How does mouse navigation performance vary across five stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, and Sham) when assessed by Time-to-Target, Success rate, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "descriptive_findings": [
    "Sham stimulation produced markedly inferior performance across all metrics: lowest Success rate (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68s), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), and lowest AD (0.236), indicating this is an effective control condition with degraded navigation.",
    "Combined stimulation yielded the highest sample size (n=48,846) and strong performance: second-highest Success rate (0.780), fastest Time-to-Target (2.56s), and highest AD (0.399), suggesting robust multisensory facilitation.",
    "Bright Visual Only and Combined paradigms showed nearly identical Success rates (0.785 vs 0.780) and similar Time-to-Target values (2.61s vs 2.56s), indicating visual stimulation alone approximates multisensory performance.",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only showed intermediate performance, with Success rates of 0.685 and 0.673 respectively, Time-to-Target around 3.05-3.14s, and comparable Path Efficiency (~0.43), suggesting unimodal stimulation provides moderate but substantially suboptimal navigation support compared to multimodal or bright visual conditions.",
    "AD showed a clear gradient: highest in Combined (0.399) and Bright Visual Only (0.387), intermediate in ICMS Only (0.354), lower in Dim Visual Only (0.336), and lowest in Sham (0.236), potentially reflecting variation in trajectory straightness or directional stability."
  ],
  "strongest_group_differences": [
    "Success rate: Sham (0.273) versus Combined/Bright Visual Only (~0.78) represents a 2.9-fold relative increase, the largest effect observed across any metric.",
    "Time-to-Target: Sham (4.68s) versus Combined (2.56s) shows an 83% increase in latency, nearly double the next-largest contrast.",
    "AD (Angular Dispersion): The Sham-to-Combined ratio of 1.69 (0.236 vs 0.399) indicates substantially more variable or curved trajectories under control conditions.",
    "Path Efficiency: Sham (0.308) versus Combined (0.502) shows a 63% relative deficit, with unimodal conditions (ICMS Only: 0.432, Dim Visual Only: 0.434) falling approximately midway."
  ],
  "practical_interpretation": "Multisensory stimulation (Combined) and bright visual stimulation produce functionally equivalent, superior navigation performance in this task, with success rates near 78% and rapid target acquisition (~2.6s). Unimodal stimulation (ICMS or dim visual) provides meaningful but substantially degraded support, reducing success rates by approximately 10-11 percentage points and increasing latency by ~20%. The Sham condition confirms that stimulation effects are genuine rather than artifactual, as absence of stimulation cripples performance (27% success, 4.7s latency). Angular dispersion patterns suggest that better-performing conditions permit straighter, more directed trajectories—possibly reflecting reduced exploratory meandering under reliable sensory guidance. These results support a dominant role for visual (especially bright) cues in mouse navigation, with ICMS providing moderate supplementary benefit only when visual input is suboptimal or absent.",
  "limitations": [
    "No inferential statistics (confidence intervals, p-values, effect sizes) are available; all comparisons are descriptive and cannot establish statistical significance.",
    "The Combined condition comprises 63.7% of all observations (48,846/76,655), creating severe imbalance that may affect precision of group comparisons and complicates variance estimation.",
    "Missing data of potential confounders (e.g., session number, training stage, individual mouse variability) precludes assessment of whether observed differences persist after controlling for repeated measures or learning effects.",
    "Path Efficiency shows extremely high variance (SD=0.47, max=29.8 vs mean=0.47), suggesting right-skewed distribution or outliers that may distort mean comparisons; median values were not provided.",
    "Interpretation of AD as angular dispersion assumes trajectory-based measurement, but the exact computational definition and its directional versus magnitude implications are not specified in the artifacts.",
    "No information on task difficulty, target distance, or environmental conditions limits contextualization of absolute performance values."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Conduct mixed-effects regression modeling with random intercepts for Mouse to account for repeated measures, using Stim Paradigm as a fixed factor; this would yield adjusted mean differences with confidence intervals and permit post-hoc pairwise comparisons with multiplicity correction. Additionally, examine distributional properties of Path Efficiency (e.g., log-transformation or robust quantile regression) given its extreme skewness, and compute standardized effect sizes (Cohen's d) for key contrasts. Finally, stratify by individual mouse to assess consistency of the Combined > Bright Visual > Unimodal > Sham hierarchy across subjects, which would strengthen causal inference about stimulation efficacy."
}
